label: Surface temperature
description: How warm the land surface itself is, like the ground under your feet. It is not the same as the air temperature a weather report gives.
why_it_matters: A warming land surface dries soil faster, stresses crops and forests, and can signal heat building up in a region.

label: Precipitation
description: How much water falls on the region in a month as rain or snow, given as the depth it would make if it stayed where it landed.
why_it_matters: Precipitation refills soil, rivers and groundwater. Changes in it are one of the main drivers of drought and flooding.

label: Soil moisture (0-10 cm)
description: How much water is held in the top 10 cm of soil. One kg of water per square metre is about 1 mm of water depth.
why_it_matters: Plants draw water from this layer, so it shows how dry or wet the land is for crops and ecosystems.

label: Evapotranspiration
description: Water moving from the land into the air, both evaporating from soil and surfaces and being released by plants.
why_it_matters: It links the water cycle and the energy cycle. It shows how much water plants and soils are returning to the atmosphere.
